claims.proposition_evaluated: Between 2025-11-18 and 2026-08-27, Administration placed before City Council or a committee of Council, on a published agenda, at least two distinct proposals to change snow and ice control service, each of whose text states new spending to deliver it. Primary readings: agenda placement by the comment date, Council or a Council committee, each separately presented service package counted once, and stated new spending.
claims.interpretation_notes: Verdict: Supported under the primary readings. Among the identified documents, P=3, C=3, U=0: (1) Parking Ban Enforcement Strategies and Resource Allocation, DocumentId 278877, states $100,000 ongoing in 2026 for contracted towing during parking bans; (2) Improved Accessibility - Active Pathway Snow Removal and Sidewalk Repair, DocumentId 278877, states new spending, including a $2.11 million one-time capital investment and 2026 operating amounts that conflict internally: the component description totals $7.83 million ($1.60M + $1.64M + $4.59M), while the table totals $9.938 million; (3) Well Maintained City, DocumentId 304812, describes winter service changes and states approximately $23.6 million ongoing operating and $11.5 million one-time capital for a broader winter and complementary seasonal package. The 24 enhancements in Attachment 10 are counted as separately costed options under the alternative unit, not as another primary service package. The August 31, 2026 committee agenda was captured by the Internet Archive on August 22, before the comment date; the committee did not consider the item until August 31. Required alternatives: considered-by-body timing through 2026-08-27: P=2, C=2, U=0, Supported. Window through 2026-10-02: identified P=3, C=3, U=0, Supported under either timing rule, since the committee considered CO03513 on August 31. Pre-election start: CO03079 is an earlier version of the active-pathway package, counted once; the identified proposals still give P at least 3, C at least 3, U=0, Supported, but the exact total is not established by the supplied meeting records. Council alone: P=2, C=2, U=0, Supported; CO03513 first reached Council after the comment date. Separately costed options: identified P=27, C=27, U=0, Supported (two Fall 2025 packages, the Well Maintained City package, and 24 Attachment 10 options). Stricter cost reading requiring an identified approved budget and stated increase: P=3, C=0, U=0, Contradicted; the counted proposal texts do not establish that comparison. Exactly-two rule: identified P=3, C=3, U=0, Partially supported. These changes make the result definition-sensitive. The primary result establishes published agenda placement under the brief's definition; it does not establish that Council approved funding or that the Well Maintained City package had been formally submitted for a budget decision. The exact total may be higher because the supplied records do not constitute a complete search of every agenda in every required window.

limitations: The report and attachment text comes from the carried public-document registry; reviewers received the same archived text, so that evidence is not independent retrieval.

The CO03513 agenda's pre-comment publication date relies on the Internet Archive capture and digest supplied in the brief. The listed live DocumentIds differ from the archived IDs, and the archived files could not be compared with the live files here.

The supplied Council and committee pages are selected items, not complete meeting pages, and do not provide a complete search of every Council and committee agenda in the required windows. The counts are for identified proposals; the exact total, especially for the pre-election window, is not established.

FCS03158 Attachment 2 was carried in selected sections rather than as a complete 144-page document. Its complete snow-related sections include the relevant identified packages; the replacement page 53 concerns the River Valley Trail Strategy and does not identify another snow proposal.
CO03513's $23.6 million ongoing and $11.5 million one-time totals cover a broader winter and complementary seasonal service package. They are not a snow-only cost allocation.

The report text for the active-pathway package gives a $2.11 million one-time capital figure, but the carried materials do not reconcile it with the separate operating table or establish an approved-budget baseline.

Whether the City states an approved snow and ice control budget baseline and an increase against it in any other source.

calculations_needed: The active-pathway package's stated components sum to $1.60M + $1.64M + $4.59M = $7.83M; its table states $9.938M. The difference is $2.108M by calculation, and no reconciliation is inferred.
Under the separately costed options alternative, Attachment 10 lists 24 enhancements; adding the two identified Fall 2025 packages and the Well Maintained City package gives 27 identified units.
what_would_change_my_verdict: Evidence that fewer than two of the identified Fall 2025 packages were listed on a published agenda by the comment date, or that either package did not propose a snow-service change or state new spending.
A complete meeting and agenda search showing a material change to the required alternative counts or the exact number of proposals.

If the primary definition were changed to require a formal funding submission or Council funding approval, CO03513 would not qualify on the evidence supplied and the question would need to be re-evaluated under that definition.
claims.suggested_one_line: Supported under the published-agenda rule: at least three identified costed service packages had been placed on Council or committee agendas by August 27, 2026, though one was presented for information ahead of formal budget deliberations.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Under the brief's rule that a proposal is put to a body when it appears on a published agenda, the identified record supports at least three costed packages: parking-ban towing, active-pathway snow removal and sidewalk repair, and Well Maintained City. The last was on the August 31 committee agenda by August 22 but was not considered until after the comment date. None of the in-window proposals establishes an increase over an identified approved snow budget.
suggested_tldr: Primary reading: Supported; three identified costed packages, with the exact total subject to a complete agenda search.
Considered by a body by August 27: two identified packages; Supported.
Council alone by August 27: two identified packages; Supported.
Stricter approved-budget comparison: Contradicted; exactly-two rule: Partially supported.
